minutes.headline: Planning Board denied the 101 Pleasant St road-length waiver and continued three hearings; Embers got a seat-capped waiver.
minutes.summary: The board waived site plan approval for Embers Pizzeria's second floor on condition of a deed restriction on seats. It denied the dead-end road length waiver for the 101 Pleasant Street subdivision and continued that hearing, 757 Chase Road and 711 Mass Ave. It also discussed a resident's two-family bylaw idea and the master plan solicitation.

public_comment.topic: Mr. Bittner asked procedural questions about 101 Pleasant Street.
Dave Mackey asked for time to discuss his two-family proposal.
Ms. Adams and Mr. Bittner advised basing the Embers restriction on seats and recording concerns on a site plan.
Ms. Adams (for an abutter) and Mr. Bittner opposed the road length waiver, citing public interest and developer profit.
Ms. Adams asked whether the applicant should withdraw; Mr. Bittner asked for standing document access and sharing with Conservation.
Mr. Bittner and Ms. Adams commented on density and accessory dwellings.
Ms. Adams advised on master plan visioning and procurement.
Dave Mackey said it was odd the select board voted no without explanation.

what_happened.line: The Planning Board denied a waiver from the dead-end road length regulation for the 101 Pleasant Street subdivision, by roll call, then repeated the motion citing the code section.
The 101 Pleasant Street hearing was continued to June 28, with a time-waiver form filed with the town clerk and staff to report the days left on the clock.
The board waived site plan approval for Embers Pizzeria's second floor at 84 Lakefront Ave, on condition of a deed restriction limiting seats.
Hearings for 757 Chase Road (to June 7) and 711 Massachusetts Avenue (to June 28) were continued.
A resident's two-family bylaw proposal was placed on the May 24 agenda, and the master plan solicitation, a bid or an RFP, was discussed without a resolution.

why_it_matters: The road length denial and the continuances leave the 101 Pleasant Street subdivision, 757 Chase Road and 711 Massachusetts Avenue undecided, so neighbors of each will see them again at the June meetings.
The seat cap is a deed restriction, so it stays with the Embers property and limits its use after this vote.
The master plan procurement method is still unsettled, and it determines how the town picks a consultant and what it spends on the plan.
watch_next: May 24: the two-family bylaw proposal (materials due by the 18th) and comments on the master plan selection criteria.
June 7 (757 Chase Road) and June 28 (101 Pleasant Street and 711 Massachusetts Avenue) hearings.
